questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle, if the uncertainty in position of an electron is zero ($\Delta x = 0$), what is the uncertainty in its momentum ($\Delta p$)?
questions.explanation: By the Heisenberg Uncertainty relation $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$. If $\Delta x = 0$, then $\Delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi \times 0} = \infty$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the hybridization of the central sulfur atom and the molecular geometry of sulfur tetrafluoride ($\text{SF}_4$)?
questions.explanation: Sulfur has 6 valence electrons. In $\text{SF}_4$, sulfur forms 4 single $\sigma$-bonds with fluorine and retains 1 lone pair. Total steric number $= 4 + 1 = 5$, indicating $sp^3d$ hybridization with a see-saw molecular geometry.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the redox reaction $\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{Fe}^{2+} + 8\text{H}^+ \to \text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Fe}^{3+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$, the equivalent weight of $\text{KMnO}_4$ in acidic medium is (where $M$ is molar mass):
questions.explanation: In acidic solution, $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ is reduced to $\text{Mn}^{2+}$, undergoing a change in oxidation state of $\Delta = 7 - 2 = 5$. Equivalent weight $= \frac{\text{Molar Mass}}{\text{Valence factor}} = \frac{M}{5}$.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: States of Matter: Gases and Liquids
questions.question: Under Graham's Law of Effusion, if methane gas ($\text{CH}_4$, $M = 16$) diffuses at a rate of $20\text{ mL/s}$, at what rate will sulfur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$, $M = 64$) diffuse under identical conditions?
questions.explanation: $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}} \implies \frac{20}{r_{\text{SO}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{64}{16}} = \sqrt{4} = 2 \implies r_{\text{SO}_2} = \frac{20}{2} = 10\text{ mL/s}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the reversible gas reaction $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g)$, what is the mathematical relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$?
questions.explanation: The relation is $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$. Here, moles of gaseous products $= 2$ and reactants $= 1 + 3 = 4$. Thus $\Delta n_g = 2 - 4 = -2$. Hence $K_p = K_c (RT)^{-2}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name for the organic compound $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$?
questions.explanation: The longest carbon chain with the principal functional group $(-\text{CHO})$ contains 4 carbons (butanal). Numbering begins at the carbonyl carbon $(C1)$. The methyl branch is at carbon-3. Thus, 3-methylbutanal.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many grams of pure sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$, molar mass $= 40\text{ g/mol}$) are required to prepare $250\text{ mL}$ of a $0.2\text{ M}$ solution?
questions.explanation: $\text{Mass } (w) = \frac{M \times V_{\text{mL}} \times \text{Molar Mass}}{1000} = \frac{0.2 \times 250 \times 40}{1000} = \frac{2000}{1000} = 2.0\text{ g}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Given the standard reduction potentials $E^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = -0.76\text{ V}$ and $E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34\text{ V}$, the standard EMF of the galvanic Daniel cell is:
questions.explanation: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) - E^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}) = (+0.34) - (-0.76) = +1.10\text{ V}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A first-order chemical reaction has a rate constant $k = 6.93 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$. What is the half-life period ($t_{1/2}$) of this reaction?
questions.explanation: For a first order reaction, $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k} = \frac{0.693}{6.93 \times 10^{-3}} = 100\text{ seconds}$.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following organic carbonyl compounds will NOT undergo the Cannizzaro reaction when treated with concentrated alkali ($50\%\text{ NaOH}$)?
questions.explanation: The Cannizzaro reaction is given only by aldehydes lacking an $\alpha$-hydrogen atom. Acetaldehyde contains three acidic $\alpha$-hydrogens, so it undergoes Aldol condensation instead of the Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Werner's coordination theory, which of the following cobalt complexes will precipitate 3 moles of $\text{AgCl}$ when treated with excess silver nitrate solution?
questions.explanation: Only chlorine atoms present in the outer ionization sphere precipitate as $\text{AgCl}$. In $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3$, all 3 chloride ions are outside the brackets in the ionization sphere, yielding $3\text{ moles of AgCl}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In proteins, the primary structure is maintained exclusively by which type of chemical bond connecting amino acid residues?

A physical blend of two or more substances.

questions.subject: Chemistry

options.text: To determine the concentration of a solution.
To identify the chemical structure of a compound.
To measure the mass of reactants.
To analyze the physical properties of substances.

questions.explanation: The primary objective of volumetric analysis is to determine the concentration of a solution through titration methods, allowing for quantitative analysis of reactants involved in a chemical reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following units is used to express molarity?
questions.explanation: Molarity is defined as the number of moles of solute per liter of solution, which is expressed in the unit moles per liter (mol/L).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If 0.5 moles of NaCl are dissolved in 2 liters of solution, what is the molarity of the solution?
questions.explanation: Molarity is calculated using the formula M = moles of solute / liters of solution. Therefore, M = 0.5 moles / 2 L = 0.25 mol/L.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a titration experiment, what is indicated by the equivalence point?

options.text: The reaction has gone to completion.
The end point has been reached.

questions.explanation: The equivalence point in a titration indicates that the amount of titrant added is stoichiometrically equivalent to the amount of analyte in the solution, meaning the reaction has gone to completion.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the purpose of standardizing a solution?
questions.explanation: Standardizing a solution is done to determine its exact concentration, which is crucial for accurate titration results and quantitative chemical analysis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following substances is a common acid-base indicator?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a redox titration, what occurs at the endpoint?

options.text: The oxidizing agent is fully reduced.
The reducing agent is fully oxidized.

questions.explanation: At the endpoint of a redox titration, the oxidizing agent is fully reduced, indicating that the reaction has reached completion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If 25.0 mL of 0.1 M NaOH is required to neutralize 50.0 mL of HCl, what is the concentration of the HCl solution?
questions.explanation: Using the equation M1V1 = M2V2, where M1 is the molarity of NaOH and V1 is its volume, the molarity of HCl can be calculated. Thus, 0.1 M x 25 mL = M2 x 50 mL, leading to M2 = 0.050 M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What could be a potential source of error in volumetric analysis?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the law of conservation of mass, what happens to mass during a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: The law of conservation of mass states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; it remains constant. This means that the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements best reflects the law of definite proportions?

options.text: Elements can combine in multiple ratios.
A compound contains the same elements in fixed proportions.

questions.explanation: The law of definite proportions asserts that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed ratio by mass, regardless of the size or source of the sample.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Gay-Lussac's law, when gases react, the volumes of the reacting gases and the volumes of the products are in what kind of ratio?
questions.explanation: Gay-Lussac's law states that when gases react at constant temperature and pressure, the volumes of the reactants and products can be expressed as simple whole number ratios, reflecting their relative amounts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many grams are in 2 moles of water (H2O)? (Molar mass of H2O = 18 g/mol)
questions.explanation: To find the mass of 2 moles of water, multiply the number of moles by the molar mass: 2 moles × 18 g/mol = 36 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a reaction between 4 moles of A and 3 moles of B, if A requires 2 moles of B to completely react, which reagent is the limiting reagent?
questions.explanation: In this reaction, 4 moles of A would require 8 moles of B for complete reaction, but only 3 moles are available. Thus, B is the limiting reagent.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If the balanced equation for a reaction indicates that 5 moles of product can be formed from the limiting reagent, what is the theoretical yield in grams if the molar mass of the product is 40 g/mol?
questions.explanation: The theoretical yield can be calculated by multiplying the number of moles of product by its molar mass: 5 moles × 40 g/mol = 200 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If the theoretical yield of a reaction is 150 g and the actual yield is 120 g, what is the percentage yield?
questions.explanation: Percentage yield is calculated using the formula: (actual yield / theoretical yield) × 100. Thus, (120 g / 150 g) × 100 = 80%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the molarity of a solution containing 5 moles of solute in 2 liters of solution?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Polyethene is formed by polymerization of:
questions.explanation: Ethene molecules undergo addition polymerization to form polyethene.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which branch of chemistry deals specifically with the study of heat and energy changes accompanying chemical reactions?
questions.explanation: Thermochemistry is the branch of physical chemistry that focuses on the heat energy absorbed or released during chemical transformations.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to the law of reciprocal proportions, if elements A and B combine separately with a fixed mass of element C, their combining ratio is:

options.text: Always identical to the sum of their atomic masses
Either the same or a simple multiple of the ratio in which they combine directly
Inversely proportional to the cube of their molecular masses
Completely independent of their direct combination ratio

questions.explanation: Jeremias Richter's Law of Reciprocal Proportions states that the ratio in which two elements combine with a fixed mass of a third element is either the same or a simple integral multiple of the ratio in which they combine with each other.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which quantum number primarily determines the spatial orientation of an atomic orbital in a magnetic field?
questions.explanation: The magnetic quantum number ($m_l$) designates the orientation of the orbital in space relative to an external magnetic coordinate system and takes values from $-l$ to $+l$.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodic Table
questions.subtopic: Historical development of the periodic table
questions.question: Along a period from left to right in the modern periodic table, atomic radius generally decreases because of:

options.text: Increase in the principal quantum number
Increase in effective nuclear charge with constant shielding
Decrease in the number of valence electrons
Increase in mutual screening among electrons

questions.explanation: Across a period, electrons are added to the same main energy shell while nuclear charge increases, increasing effective nuclear pull ($Z_{eff}$) and pulling valence electrons closer to the nucleus.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following molecules has a trigonal bipyramidal geometry according to VSEPR theory?
questions.explanation: $\text{PCl}_5$ has 5 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs around the central phosphorus atom ($sp^3d$ hybridization), resulting in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the oxidation state of chromium in the dichromate ion, $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$?
questions.explanation: In $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$, $2x + 7(-2) = -2 \implies 2x - 14 = -2 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = +6$.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: States of Matter: Gases and Liquids
questions.question: Under what conditions do real gases behave most like an ideal gas?
questions.explanation: At low pressures and high temperatures, intermolecular forces become negligible and molecular volume is tiny compared to total container volume, adhering to ideal gas assumptions.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the exothermic synthesis of ammonia $\text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g) + \text{Heat}$, Le Chatelier's principle predicts that equilibrium yield of $\text{NH}_3$ increases with:

options.text: Adding an inert gas at constant volume

questions.explanation: Because the forward reaction produces fewer moles of gas ($4 \to 2$) and releases heat ($\Delta H < 0$), higher pressure shifts equilibrium forward and lower temperature favors exothermic heat generation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What volume of $0.1\text{ M HCl}$ is required to neutralize exactly $25\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M NaOH}$?
questions.explanation: Using $M_1V_1 = M_2V_2$ for monoprotic neutralization: $(0.1\text{ M}) \times V_1 = (0.2\text{ M}) \times (25\text{ mL}) \implies V_1 = 5.0 / 0.1 = 50.0\text{ mL}$.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The solubility product constant ($K_{sp}$) of a sparingly soluble binary salt $AB$ is $1.0 \times 10^{-10}$. What is its molar solubility in pure water?
questions.explanation: For $AB(s) \rightleftharpoons A^+(aq) + B^-(aq)$, $K_{sp} = s^2$. Hence $s = \sqrt{K_{sp}} = \sqrt{1.0 \times 10^{-10}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ M}$.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For a zero-order chemical reaction, what are the SI units of the rate constant ($k$)?
questions.explanation: For an $n$-th order reaction, the unit of $k$ is $(\text{mol/L})^{1-n}\text{s}^{-1}$. For $n = 0$, the unit is $\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which thermodynamic parameter must be negative for a reaction to proceed spontaneously under constant temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: According to the second law of thermodynamics, a chemical process is spontaneous at constant $T$ and $P$ if and only if $\Delta G < 0$.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Oxidation and reduction in electrochemical systems
questions.question: During the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride ($	ext{NaCl}$) using inert platinum electrodes, which gas is liberated at the anode?
questions.explanation: Due to the lower overpotential of chloride oxidation compared to water oxidation, chloride ions discharge preferentially at the anode to produce chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$).
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which alkyl halide mechanism proceeds with complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion)?
questions.explanation: The bimolecular nucleophilic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}2$) involves concerted backside nucleophilic attack, leading to complete stereochemical inversion of the tetrahedral carbon.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Lucas reagent, used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols, consists of:
questions.explanation: Lucas reagent is an equimolar solution of anhydrous zinc chloride in concentrated hydrochloric acid, forming insoluble alkyl chlorides with tertiary alcohols immediately.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds gives a positive Tollens' silver mirror test?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes like acetaldehyde are readily oxidized by ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent) to precipitate metallic silver, whereas ketones do not react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following best defines chemistry?

options.text: The study of matter and its changes.
The study of the Earth's physical structure.

questions.explanation: Chemistry is fundamentally defined as the study of matter and its changes, which includes the examination of substances and their transformations. This definition encompasses all branches of chemistry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Importance of chemistry in daily life
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an application of chemistry in daily life?
questions.explanation: While cooking, cleaning agents, and medicinal drugs all involve chemical processes and substances, studying ancient civilizations does not directly involve chemistry as a discipline.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which branch of chemistry focuses on the composition and structure of substances?
questions.explanation: Analytical Chemistry is specifically concerned with the composition, structure, and properties of substances, using various techniques to analyze material samples.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a mixture?

options.text: Can be separated by physical means.

questions.explanation: A mixture can be separated into its components using physical methods, contrasting with pure substances that have fixed compositions and properties.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the primary difference between an element and a compound?

options.text: Elements can be broken down chemically.
Compounds are made of two or more elements.
Elements contain two or more types of atoms.

questions.explanation: The primary distinction is that a compound consists of two or more different elements chemically combined, whereas an element is a pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about ions?

options.text: Ions are created when atoms gain or lose electrons.
Ions are only found in solid form.

questions.explanation: Ions are charged species that form when atoms either lose or gain electrons. This charge imbalance is what distinguishes them from neutral atoms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: How many molecules are present in one mole of a substance?
questions.explanation: One mole of any substance contains Avogadro's number of molecules, which is approximately 6.022 x 10^23. This constant is fundamental in stoichiometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What do coefficients in a balanced chemical equation represent?

options.text: The number of moles of reactants and products.
The temperature at which the reaction occurs.

questions.explanation: Coefficients in a balanced chemical equation indicate the relative number of moles of each substance involved in the reaction, ensuring the law of conservation of mass is upheld.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In a balanced chemical equation, which principle is primarily utilized?
questions.explanation: The balancing of chemical equations is fundamentally based on the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the molarity of a solution prepared by dissolving 5 grams of NaCl in enough water to make 250 mL of solution? (Molar mass of NaCl = 58.5 g/mol)
questions.explanation: To find molarity (M), use the formula M = moles of solute / liters of solution. First, calculate moles of NaCl: 5 g / 58.5 g/mol = 0.0855 moles. Convert 250 mL to liters: 250 mL = 0.250 L. M = 0.0855 moles / 0.250 L = 0.342 M, which rounds to 0.34 M.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.
